rule: prose contradicts a proposition's sign (prop:att_cs(i), prop:comparative_statics(ii), cor:rho)
claim: Section 2 and Conclusion say fewer EPC-sensitive buyers make hiding more attractive; the model says the opposite.
evidence: Section 2 L86-87: "a demand side in which many buyers do not price the attribute weakens the penalty that would otherwise discipline them"; main.tex L343 Conclusion (rewritten 2026-11-03): "buyer heterogeneity makes exploiting that ambiguity financially worthwhile". P2 and P5 independently derive d sigma0*/d rho > 0 (sympy; formula theta-bar(1-pi)/[c0 pi (1-theta-bar)]).
failing_case: pi .5, theta-bar .6, beta1 10, omega1 1, psi .5, e^def 2.3, c0 7: as rho goes .485, .49, .50, .51, sigma0* goes .057, .192, .500, .870 and Delta* stays 7.000.
suggested_fix: Restate the rho channel as the revenue channel: more sensitive buyers raise b, Delta in the corners and sigma0*.

rule: state which results rest on the functional form
claim: The appendix scopes the dependence on linear pricing to the equilibrium propositions; the inversion e-tilde = Delta/b, psi-hat_delta and Prop att_identification also need it.
evidence: A-attention L408: "all propositions of Section ss:att_equilibrium".
failing_case: Exact three-segment logit (V-bar 12, zeta^ins 1, rho .5, omega1 1, zeta0 3, zeta1 1, e .6, zeta^def 0): at psi = .13 exact ratio 1.239 vs linear 1.383; plugging 1.239 into the linear inversion gives psi-hat .29, true .13.
suggested_fix: Extend the caveat to Sections 4.4 and 4.5.

rule: claim must match the reported Monte Carlo
claim: "This biases both estimators toward full attention" is wrong for the regression through the origin and not general for the ratio of sums.
evidence: macros_mc: regression through the origin 0.33-0.70 without selection, 0.30-0.60 with. Same wording at L461, L480 (Fig F3b caption).
failing_case: Houses (psi .95, e .59, eta 2.11, s_L 3, s_H .3): Monte Carlo .951 without selection, .936 with, i.e. away from 1.
suggested_fix: State the sign condition; limit the claim to the ratio of sums in apartments.

rule: summary parity between body and appendix
claim: Appendix reads bound violations as evidence of a second force; body says about half would exceed it from sampling error alone.
evidence: A-attention L470 "40 percent of markets in the top tercile also exceed it ... probably not the only one" vs 04-structural L590 "does not point to a second force".
failing_case: 21/45 = 47% overall and 40% in the top tercile are at or below the roughly 50% the body attributes to noise.
suggested_fix: Author chooses one reading and states it in both places.

rule: every proof step must be true
claim: Step 3 says the belief after silence is the limit of the pool belief as pi -> 1; along the PP path e* does not depend on pi, so the limit is e*, not 0, and Step 5 calls the premium discontinuous at pi = 1, which needs belief 0.
evidence: A-attention L651, L661. Numerically the pool belief stays .5800 at pi .5, .9, .99, .999 while sigma0* falls .207 -> .0002.
failing_case: Conclusion survives by the intuitive criterion (high type best-case gain -3.88, equilibrium-dominated; low type +0.22) but the proof does not show it.
suggested_fix: Drop the limit argument; prove the domination inequality b psi (1 - e*) < b.

rule: proposition and its use must refer to the same object
claim: The saving bound covers the average of seller-specific S_i*, but the text reads it as the saving to the state against a bill paying one S*_m per market.
evidence: main.tex L316, L331, L335 and the bill at L234.
failing_case: Apartment-like inputs (costs 4.5 + Exp(25), sigma0-hat .151, R-hat 3): average fall .173, bound .452; market-uniform full-take-up subsidy falls by 2.99, 6.6 times the bound.
suggested_fix: State that transfers are seller-specific or bound the uniform-subsidy saving separately.

rule: statement must hold under the model's own primitives
claim: prop:premium ignores c0 and covers K = 0 sellers who cannot disclose.
evidence: A-benchmark L19-23: "(K,theta) strictly prefers disclosure iff theta > e(sigma0*)"; "(ii) theta = 0 strictly prefers non-disclosure whenever e > 0".
failing_case: pi = theta-bar = rho = .5, beta1 = 1, c0 = .3: CDH, e* = .5 > 0, low type net gain from silence -.05, strictly prefers disclosure, contradicting (ii) and prop:equilibrium(i).
suggested_fix: State it gross of hiding costs (c0 = c1 = 0) and for K = 1; 04:304 already says so.

rule: the proof must use the model in the statement
claim: Proof of prop:premium and cor:hq_disclose is built on the logit pricing model while the benchmark rests on linear pricing; Lemma A.1 is about profit but is used to compare prices.
evidence: main.tex L444-521; B:11 and A-attention:415 say the results rest on linear pricing; L506 gives "rho in [0,1] >= 0" as the reason dPi/dv1 > 0 (needs rho > 0).
failing_case: Any rho < 1: the step from v1 to price is not established (A-attention:415 itself says two-segment price monotonicity needs a cross-partial condition).
suggested_fix: Use the linear-pricing one-liner U(1,theta,0) - U(1,theta,1) = rho beta1 (e - theta) - (c0 + theta c1), or cite Prop att_incentives at psi = 1.

rule: claim must match the paper's own reported numbers
claim: The proof calls Partial Pooling "the empirically dominant regime".
evidence: A-robustness L316-320: every market in PP "by construction", no regime heterogeneity reported as a finding; \attRawNPpApt = 0 of 45 apartment and 11 of 97 house markets in PP under LA.
failing_case: Fig att_belief puts 37 of 45 apartment markets outside what the benchmark can produce.

rule: a stated prediction must be implied by the model
claim: Cross-market predictions on rho and the "expanding" band do not follow from the model.
evidence: A-benchmark L134, L144-146; main.tex L683. Simulation (c0 independent of rho, rho ~ U[.2,1], pi = theta-bar = .5): corr(rho, premium | PP) = +.93 with c0 ~ U[0,1]; P(corner | rho above median) 1.000 vs .868 below with c0 ~ U[0,.15]; band shifts [.167,.25] -> [.20,.30] from rho .5 to .6.
failing_case: At c0 = .18, raising rho from .5 to .6 moves the market from PP (sigma0* .78) into CAS.
suggested_fix: Condition the predictions on c0/(rho beta1) or drop them; describe the band as shifting up and widening.

rule: welfare claims must follow from the model
claim: "Transfer from buyers" and "pure rent" are wrong in the benchmark: buyers price the pool at its Bayesian mean, so the expected transfer is zero, and contamination costs uninformed sellers.
evidence: A-benchmark L165, same wording at main.tex L347.
failing_case: pi = theta-bar = .5, rho beta1 = .5, c0 = .2: e* = .4, sigma0* = .5; buyers pay .2 for expected value .2; uninformed sellers get .2 vs .25 with no hiding.

rule: figures must be labelled with the model that produced them
claim: Robustness is computed on the full-attention cost c0-hat^FA, which L117 says is benchmark-only, then draws conclusions about the paper's hiding cost.
evidence: A-robustness L65-102, table L36: "this is the paper's most consequential specification choice"; "read the concealment cost as the smaller figure throughout".
failing_case: LA cost has mean Delta-hat (8.5 apartments, 3.9 houses); c0-hat^FA gives 2.41 vs 3.45, reverse order; simulated mean predicted premium 6.1172 before and after a +.067 shift in e-hat*.
suggested_fix: Label every cost figure as the full-attention benchmark; add LA c0-hat and psi-hat_delta columns.

rule: one definition per symbol; identification claims must match Section 4
claim: Statements identify rho_m itself; Section 4 says the anchor identifies delta(rho omega1), and rho only under omega1 = 1.
evidence: A-robustness L109, L124-133, L226-236, L67, L300-302 ("Point identification of rho_m"; "genuine point estimate").
failing_case: (rho, omega1) = (1, .5) and (.5, 1) give the same b, Delta and rho-hat = .5 (sympy difference 0).
suggested_fix: Add omega1 = 1 to the hypotheses or restate in terms of rho omega1.

rule: hypotheses used must be in the statement
claim: plim r-hat = 1 relies on No Pre-Reform Energy Pricing and psi = 1, not stated; "about 1 regardless" is contradicted by the appendix's own data.
failing_case: PP before and after with c0 fixed gives Delta-hat -> 0, r-hat -> 0; 40 of 45 apartment markets (89%) have r-hat > 1.
suggested_fix: Add the hypotheses to the corollary and qualify L112.

claim: Appendix four-group classification contradicts Section 3: "Falsification ... (excluded)" vs Section 3 retaining disclosed-unmatched listings as truthful disclosers.
evidence: main.tex L387-407; Section 3 Table tab:groups: "Disclosed, unmatched | d=1 | K=0 | 32.2% / 51.2%". Verified by the dispatcher.
failing_case: A reader takes the appendix as the sample definition and concludes 32.2% (apartments) and 51.2% (houses) of listings are suspected misreporters excluded from estimation; the "1 | 0 or mismatch" row also overlaps the Truthful row. The table is never referenced.
suggested_fix: Delete the appendix table and point to Table tab:groups, or copy Section 3's table and note.

claim: Appendix defines K as true information status; Section 3 says K = 0 is no post-July-2021 registry record.
evidence: main.tex L380, L383-386, L410 ("directly observe the latent variable K") vs 03-setting L105.
failing_case: A reader of the appendix believes K = 0 means the seller lacks a certificate and misses the known direction of bias in sigma0-hat and psi-hat.
suggested_fix: Define K as "a certificate appears in the registry at listing time"; replace "Seller lacks information" with "no registry record".

claim: theta is the A-G score here and binary quality in the model; the cut is never given.
evidence: main.tex L381-382 vs 04-structural L40 (theta in {0,1}); appendix later uses zeta_{theta,m} with theta in {0,1}.
failing_case: A reader cannot tell what E-bar_{0,m} and E-bar_{1,m} average or whether D-rated dwellings enter (the input to beta1^anchor).
suggested_fix: Write theta in {0,1}: binary quality derived from the certified grade and give the cut.

claim: rho is a probability in (0,1) here and an unclipped effective-attention ratio in the estimates.
evidence: main.tex L421 vs 04-structural L54, L523 and the Section 4 table notes ("not clipped to [0,1]", row "Markets with rho-hat > 1").
failing_case: A reader sees a "share" with estimates above one and reads a bug.
suggested_fix: State that rho-hat equals rho omega1 under the anchor and equals rho only at omega1 = 1.

claim: Footnote promises "a full explanation of our matching strategy in the appendix"; none exists.
evidence: main.tex L383 footnote; appendix sections are robustness, rho-identification, benchmark, attention proofs, proofs.
failing_case: The matching rules (address, floor, type, area tolerances) that define K cannot be found.
suggested_fix: Add the matching appendix or cite where it lives.
